---
title: "Appendix C — Glossary"
---

This glossary defines, in alphabetical order, the central terms used across the
book. Notation follows [Appendix A](appendix-a-math.qmd); every named method is
cited to its primary source.

## A

**AUPRC.** Area under the precision–recall curve, aggregating precision
$\mathrm{TP}/(\mathrm{TP}+\mathrm{FP})$ and recall
$\mathrm{TP}/(\mathrm{TP}+\mathrm{FN})$; preferred to AUROC under class imbalance.
See Chapter 11, @eq-ch11-auprc [@saito2015precision].

**AUROC.** Area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve, equal to the
probability that a random positive is ranked above a random negative; threshold-free
but optimistic when positives are rare. See Chapter 11.

## B

**Batch effect.** Systematic technical variation between groups of samples
processed separately (day, donor, chemistry, run) that is confounded with the
biological signal and must be removed during integration. See Chapter 8
[@luecken2022benchmarking].

## C

**Calibration (ECE).** The agreement between predicted probabilities and observed
frequencies, summarised by expected calibration error; deep networks are often
overconfident. See Chapter 11, @eq-ch11-ece [@guo2017calibration].

**CLIP-style alignment.** Contrastive training of two encoders so that matched
pairs have high cosine similarity and mismatched pairs low, via an InfoNCE-style
objective on paired modalities. See Chapter 9, @eq-ch09-clip [@radford2021learning].

**Contextual embedding.** An embedding $f_\theta(x\mid\mathcal{C})$ that depends on
a token's surrounding context, as opposed to a static (feature) embedding
$f_\theta(x)$ fixed per token. See Chapter 1, @eq-ch01-contextual.

## D

**D-MPNN.** Directed message passing neural network, which passes messages over
directed bonds — avoiding the to-and-fro of undirected schemes — before a
permutation-invariant readout; the backbone of Chemprop. See Chapter 7,
@eq-ch07-dmpnn [@yang2019analyzing].

**Data leakage.** Contamination of training by information unavailable at
prediction time, so that validation overstates generalisation; in biology usually
structural (related entities in both splits). See Chapter 11 [@whalen2022navigating].

## E

**ECFP/Morgan fingerprint.** Extended-connectivity (circular) fingerprint that
hashes iterated atom environments into a fixed-length binary vector. See Chapter 7,
@eq-ch07-ecfp [@rogers2010extended].

**ELBO.** Evidence lower bound, a tractable surrogate for the log marginal
likelihood that trades a reconstruction term against a KL penalty and is maximised
to train variational autoencoders. See Chapter 3, @eq-ch03-elbo [@kingma2014auto].

**Embedding.** A parameterised map $f_\theta:\mathcal{X}\to\mathbb{R}^{d}$ sending
biological entities to vectors so that geometric relations — distances, inner
products, directions — reflect biological relations. See Appendix A and Chapter 1,
@eq-ch01-embedding.

**Equivariance.** The property that a model commutes with an input transformation,
$f(RP+\mathbf{1}t^\top)=Rf(P)+\mathbf{1}t^\top$, required for coordinate-valued
outputs under rotation and translation. See Chapter 6, @eq-ch06-equivariance
[@satorras2021n].

## F

**Feature hashing.** Mapping high-cardinality discrete features to fixed-width
vectors by a hash function, giving bounded-dimension encodings for unbounded
vocabularies such as k-mers. See Chapter 4, @eq-ch04-kmer-hash
[@weinberger2009featurehashing].

**Foundation model.** A model trained on broad data at scale, usually
self-supervised, whose representations transfer to many downstream tasks through
fine-tuning, prompting, or linear probing. See Chapter 13
[@bommasani2021opportunities].

## G

**GVP.** Geometric vector perceptron, an equivariant layer that processes scalar
and vector features so that outputs transform correctly under rotation. See
Chapter 6, @eq-ch06-gvp [@jing2021learning].

## H

**Homology split.** A train/test partition that assigns whole sequence-similarity
clusters to a single fold, so no test relative appears in training. See Chapter 11,
@eq-ch11-homology-split [@whalen2022navigating].

**HVG.** Highly variable genes, the subset of genes selected by expression variance
after normalisation to reduce dimensionality before embedding. See Chapter 8,
@eq-ch08-hvg.

## I

**InfoNCE.** The contrastive objective that maximises a softmax log-likelihood of a
positive pair against in-batch negatives; a lower bound on mutual information. See
Chapter 3, @eq-ch03-infonce [@vandenoord2018representation].

**Integrated gradients.** An attribution method that averages gradients along the
straight path from a baseline to the input, satisfying sensitivity and completeness.
See Chapter 12, @eq-ch12-integrated-gradients [@sundararajan2017axiomatic].

**Integration.** Combining embeddings from multiple datasets while removing batch
variation and preserving biological variation. See Chapter 8
[@luecken2022benchmarking].

**Invariance.** The property that a model's output is unchanged by an input
transformation, e.g. invariance to global rotation and translation for scalar
structure features. See Chapter 6, @eq-ch06-invariance [@satorras2021n].

## K

**k-mer.** A contiguous subsequence of length $k$; a sequence is represented by its
vector of k-mer counts, the biological analogue of bag-of-words. See Chapter 4,
@eq-ch04-kmer-profile.

**KL divergence.** A non-symmetric, non-negative measure $D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P\Vert Q)$
of how far a distribution $Q$ diverges from a reference $P$; central to variational
inference and t-SNE. See Appendix A, @eq-appa-kl [@kullback1951information].

**Knowledge graph.** A graph of typed entities linked by typed relations whose
atomic facts are triples $(h,r,t)$, embedded for link prediction. See Chapter 10.

## L

**Linear probe.** A low-capacity classifier (usually logistic regression) trained on
frozen embeddings to test whether a target is linearly decodable, yielding a lower
bound on recoverable information. See Chapter 11, @eq-ch11-linear-probe
[@alain2016understanding].

## M

**MACCS keys.** A fixed set of 166 structurally defined substructure keys forming a
binary substructure fingerprint. See Chapter 7 [@durant2002reoptimization].

**Masked language modeling.** A self-supervised objective that masks tokens and
trains the model to reconstruct them from bidirectional context; the BERT-style
pretraining used by many sequence language models. See Chapter 3
[@devlin2019bert].

**Message passing.** The graph-neural-network update in which each node aggregates
transformed messages from its neighbours,
$\mathbf{h}_i^{(l+1)}=U(\mathbf{h}_i^{(l)},\bigoplus_{j\in\mathcal{N}(i)}M(\cdot))$,
followed by a permutation-invariant readout. See Chapter 7, @eq-ch07-mpnn and
Chapter 10, @eq-ch10-mp [@gilmer2017neural].

**Mismatch/spectrum kernel.** String kernels comparing sequences by shared k-mers:
the spectrum kernel counts exact matches, the mismatch kernel allows up to $m$
substitutions. See Chapter 4, @eq-ch04-mismatch
[@leslie2002spectrum; @leslie2004mismatch].

**Mutual information.** The reduction in uncertainty about one variable from
observing another, $I(X;Y)=H(X)-H(X\mid Y)$; the quantity contrastive objectives
bound. See Appendix A, @eq-appa-mi [@cover2006elements].

## O

**One-hot encoding.** The indicator vector $e_a$ with a single one at the position
of category $a$; a baseline sequence encoding that ignores similarity between
categories. See Chapter 1, @eq-ch01-onehot.

## P

**Permutation invariance.** The requirement that a set-level output be unchanged by
reordering its elements, $R(\{\mathbf{h}_{\pi(i)}\})=R(\{\mathbf{h}_i\})$, as needed
for atoms, residues, and graph nodes. See Chapter 6,
@eq-ch06-permutation-invariance [@gilmer2017neural].

**Profile HMM.** A hidden Markov model built from a multiple sequence alignment that
scores a sequence against a family's position-specific match, insert, and delete
states. See Chapter 5 [@eddy2011accelerated].

**Protein language model (PLM).** A model pretrained self-supervised on large
protein-sequence corpora whose per-residue embeddings transfer to structure and
function tasks. See Chapter 5 [@rives2021biological].

**PSSM.** Position-specific scoring matrix, an $L\times 20$ matrix giving the
log-odds score of each amino acid at each position, derived from an alignment or a
PSI-BLAST profile. See Chapter 5, @eq-ch05-pssm [@altschul1997gapped].

## Q

**QSAR/QSPR.** Quantitative structure–activity (or structure–property) relationship:
predicting a molecule's activity or property from its representation. See
Chapters 7 and 14.

## R

**Representation learning.** The automatic discovery of features or latent vectors
that make downstream tasks easier, replacing hand-crafted descriptors. See
Chapter 1 [@bengio2013representation].

## S

**Scaling law.** An empirical power-law relating model size, data, and compute to
loss, used to allocate pretraining resources. See Chapter 13,
@eq-ch13-scaling-law [@kaplan2020scaling].

**scVI.** A deep generative (variational autoencoder) model of single-cell counts
that learns a latent cell embedding while correcting for batch. See Chapter 8,
@eq-ch08-scvi-likelihood [@lopez2018deep].

**SMILES.** A linear text string encoding a molecular graph, used as tokeniser input
for chemical language models. See Chapter 7 [@weininger1988smiles].

**Static (feature) embedding.** An embedding that assigns one fixed vector to each
token independent of context. See Chapter 1, @eq-ch01-contextual.

## T

**Tanimoto similarity.** The ratio
$\langle u,v\rangle/(\lVert u\rVert_1+\lVert v\rVert_1-\langle u,v\rangle)$ between
binary fingerprints, the standard chemical similarity. See Chapter 7,
@eq-ch07-tanimoto [@rogers2010extended].

**Tokenization/BPE.** Splitting a sequence into model tokens; byte-pair encoding
greedily merges frequent substrings into a subword vocabulary, trading vocabulary
size against sequence length. See Chapter 4 [@sennrich2016neural].

**TM-score.** A length-normalised structural-alignment similarity in $[0,1]$
measuring how well two folds superimpose. See Chapter 6 [@zhang2005tmalign].

**TransE/RotatE.** Knowledge-graph embedding models scoring a triple $(h,r,t)$ by
translation ($h+r\approx t$) or by rotation in complex space. See Chapter 10,
@eq-ch10-transe and @eq-ch10-rotate [@bordes2013translating; @sun2019rotate].

**t-SNE.** A nonlinear dimensionality-reduction method that minimises the KL
divergence between high- and low-dimensional neighbour distributions; good for
clusters, unreliable for global distances. See Chapter 2, @eq-ch02-tsne-obj
[@vandermaaten2008visualizing].

**Trustworthiness.** A rank-based measure of how many neighbour pairs preserved in a
low-dimensional visualization were also neighbours in the original space. See
Chapter 12, @eq-ch12-trustworthiness [@kaski2003trustworthiness].

## U

**UMAP.** A manifold-learning method that builds a fuzzy neighbour graph and
optimises a cross-entropy between high- and low-dimensional graphs; faster than
t-SNE and preserving more global structure. See Chapter 2, @eq-ch02-umap-obj
[@mcinnes2018umap].

## Z

**ZINB.** Zero-inflated negative binomial distribution, a count likelihood modelling
both over-dispersion and an excess of zeros, as used by scVI. See Chapter 8,
@eq-ch08-zinb [@lopez2018deep].
